papers.title: Mesoscopic evolution of molten pool during selective laser melting of superalloy Inconel 738 at elevating preheating temperature
papers.abstract: Due to the poor weldability of Inconel 738 alloy, defects (cracks, pores) always exist in the selective laser melting(SLM) process. In this paper, the molten pool evolution of the single track, including the morphology, porosity and crack formation, was systematically investigated by numerical simulation, and the effects of different preheating temperature and process parameters were verified by experimental analysis. The detailed temperature-dependent thermal physical properties were applied into the Volume of Fluid (VOF) method to simulate a powder bed computational domain which was established by Discrete Element Model (DEM). The simulation results show that the change of molten pool width by different laser power and preheating was not as significant as that of depth. The results also demonstrate that higher energy density and preheating temperature induced the generation of pores at the bottom of molten pool, which can be explained by the variation in cooling rates . Moreover, the change of temperature gradients in three-dimensional directions with the increase of preheating temperature was also investigated, which explained the reason for crack forming and extending through the center line. Finally, the evolution of molten pool at a higher preheating temperature 1000℃ was simulated to further underpin the positive effect of preheating on preventing cracks formation.

llm.relevance_to_user: 该论文研究高温合金Inconel 738的选区激光熔化工艺，完全不涉及生物医学植入物的力学性能或骨整合。
llm.why_not_core: The paper focuses on nickel-based superalloy additive manufacturing with no biomedical context, no porous structure design, no stress shielding evaluation, no fatigue testing, and no osseointegration consideration.

summary_zh.motivation: 研究预热温度对Inconel 738合金SLM熔池演化和缺陷形成的影响。
summary_zh.method: 采用VOF和DEM模拟熔池动态，并通过单道实验验证工艺参数影响。
summary_zh.result: 预热降低冷却速率和温度梯度，减少裂纹但增加底部气孔风险。
summary_zh.validation: 通过单道实验对比熔池形态和缺陷进行验证。

summary_en.motivation: To investigate the effect of preheating temperature on molten pool evolution and defect formation during selective laser melting of Inconel 738 superalloy.
summary_en.method: A numerical model combining Volume of Fluid and Discrete Element Method was used to simulate molten pool dynamics, validated by single-track experiments with varying preheating and laser parameters.
summary_en.result: Preheating reduced cooling rate and temperature gradients, suppressing cracks but increasing porosity at the melt pool bottom under higher energy density.
summary_en.validation: Experimental single-track deposition was used to validate simulation predictions of melt pool geometry and defect formation.

papers.title: Advantages and issues of concern regarding approaches to peripheral nerve block for total hip arthroplasty
papers.abstract: In older patients with comorbidities, hip fractures are both an important and debilitating condition. Since multimodal and multidisciplinary perioperative strategies can hasten functional recovery after surgery improving clinical outcomes, the choice of the most effective and safest pathway represents a great challenge. A key point of concern is the anesthetic approach and above all the choice of the locoregional anesthesia combined with general or neuraxial anesthesia.

papers.title: Influence of 17-4 PH stainless steel powder recycling on properties of SLM additive manufactured parts
papers.abstract: Metal Additive Manufacturing (AM) processes are developing quickly. These processes have several attractive qualities, however, the quality of manufactured parts still remains a major issue that needs to be addressed if it is to become a prevalent technology in the industry. In some powder bed fusion techniques, such as Selective Laser Melting (SLM), there is a portion of initial powder that does not melt and it can be recycled to ensure the economic and environmental viability of the process. In previous research, we demonstrated the morphological, chemical and microstructural change suffered by 17-4 PH stainless steel powder after reusing it in a SLM manufacturing process. In this work, the properties of 17-4 PH stainless steel parts, printed from powder in different recycling states (virgin powder (P0) and 20 times reused powder (P20)), were evaluated, in order to establish good recycling procedures and optimise the SLM process performance. Analyses of the properties revealed a slight decrease in roughness and pore size with powder recycling. The external porosity of the samples is similar in both powder states; however, internal porosity decreases by increasing the number of reuse cycles. Regarding the microstructural analysis, a slight increase in the γ-phase is observed with the powder recycling, which leads to a slight increase in ductility and decrease in hardness of the samples. Therefore, it is concluded that the 17-4 PH powder recycling process in SLM manufacturing is adequate and recommended to ensure the economic and environmental viability of the process without adversely affecting the properties of the parts.

llm.why_not_core: This paper does not cover any biomedical implant application, porous structure design for stress shielding, fatigue testing, or osseointegration evaluation relevant to the user's direction.

summary_zh.motivation: 评估粉末回收对SLM零件性能的影响以优化工艺经济性。
summary_zh.method: 对比原始粉末与20次回收粉末所制样品的性能，包括粗糙度、孔隙率、显微组织等。
summary_zh.result: 回收导致粗糙度和孔隙率轻微下降，γ相增加，延展性提高，硬度降低。
summary_zh.validation: 通过微观表征和力学测试验证回收粉末的适用性。

summary_en.motivation: The paper aims to evaluate the effect of powder recycling on the properties of SLM-fabricated 17-4PH stainless steel parts to ensure economic and environmental viability.
summary_en.method: Properties of parts printed from virgin powder and powder reused 20 times were compared, including surface roughness, porosity, microstructure, and mechanical properties.
summary_en.result: Recycling led to slight decreases in roughness and pore size, an increase in γ-phase content, enhanced ductility, and reduced hardness.
summary_en.validation: Validation was performed through microstructural analysis and mechanical testing (hardness, ductility) on as-built samples.
